name: gcloud
label: Google Cloud
description: Google Cloud for the agent — read projects, Compute Engine VMs, Cloud Run services, Storage buckets and objects, Cloud SQL instances, GKE clusters, Cloud Functions, log entries and billing status; and start, stop or reset a VM. Authenticates with its own service-account key, so it sees exactly what that account's IAM roles allow and never borrows anyone's Google login.
author: TheBananaStand

descriptor.details: Reads Google Cloud through its own service-account key, so it sees exactly what that account's IAM roles allow — roles/viewer for everything read-only, plus roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 if you want Leo to be able to start and stop VMs. Nobody's personal Google login is involved, and object contents are never downloaded.
descriptor.setup_hint: In Google Cloud: IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → create one, grant it roles/viewer, then Keys → Add key → JSON. Paste the file's contents below.
use_cases: What's running in the prod project right now?
Show me the last hour of errors from the API service.
Stop the build box — I'm done with it.
Is billing still attached to that project?

sends.purpose: A one-hour assertion signed with your service-account key, exchanged for a short-lived access token. The key itself never leaves this box; the assertion names only the service account and the scope it asks for.
The access token, to list the projects that service account can see. Nothing of yours travels with it.
The access token and a project id to list VMs — and, only when you ask to start, stop or reset one, that instance's name and zone. No disk or VM contents are read.
The access token, a project id and a region, to list Cloud Run services and the images they run.
The access token, a project id, and the bucket name and name prefix you ask about. Object contents are never downloaded or sent — only names, sizes and types come back.
The access token and a project id, to list Cloud SQL instances. No database connection is made and no data is read.
The access token and a project id, to list GKE clusters and their versions.
The access token and a project id, to list Cloud Functions and their runtimes.

The access token, a project id, a time window, and the log filter. Claude writes that filter from your conversation, so it can quote what you said — but no transcript, file or other package's data is attached.
The access token and a project id, to read which billing account the project is attached to and whether billing is enabled. No invoices, amounts or payment details are requested.
